ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, B, C, D are on the same horizontal straight line, triangle ABC is above BC, and triangle ECD is above CD. The shaded quadrilateral ABCE can be composed of triangle ABC and triangle ACE, with AC as the dividing line between them. Reasoning: It is known that ABC is an equilateral triangle with side length 2, so AC=2, and area(ABC)=(sqrt(3)/4)*2^2=sqrt(3). ECD is an equilateral triangle with side length 1, so CE=1. Since BC and CD are collinear, and both equilateral triangles are on the same side of this straight line, rays CA and CE form an angle of 60° at point C. Therefore area(ACE)=(1/2)*AC*CE*sin60°=(1/2)*2*1*(sqrt(3)/2)=sqrt(3)/2. The area of quadrilateral ABCE is sqrt(3)+sqrt(3)/2=3sqrt(3)/2.

method.method_draft: Decompose the shaded quadrilateral into two triangles: triangle ABC and triangle ACE. From the image, B, C, and D lie on one straight horizontal line, with equilateral triangle ABC built above BC and equilateral triangle ECD built above CD; quadrilateral ABCE consists of triangle ABC plus the connecting triangle ACE. From the text, ABC has side 2 and ECD has side 1, so AC=2 and CE=1. Since ABC and ECD are equilateral and their bases BC and CD are collinear, the rays CA and CE make a 60-degree angle at C. Compute area(ABC) = (sqrt(3)/4)*2^2 = sqrt(3), and area(ACE) = (1/2)(2)(1)sin 60° = sqrt(3)/2. Add them to get 3sqrt(3)/2.

method.method_draft: Use coordinates and the shoelace formula. From the image, place the common baseline horizontally with B=(0,0), C=(2,0), and D=(3,0). From the text, ABC is equilateral of side 2, so its top vertex is A=(1,sqrt(3)). Also ECD is equilateral of side 1 on CD, so E=(2.5,sqrt(3)/2). Now apply the shoelace formula to quadrilateral A-B-C-E in that order. The signed double area is |1*0+0*0+2*(sqrt(3)/2)+(5/2)*sqrt(3) - (sqrt(3)*0+0*2+0*(5/2)+(sqrt(3)/2)*1)| = 3sqrt(3). Therefore the area is 3sqrt(3)/2.
